# PERSONASHIFTAI ? FULL-STACK INTEGRATION MASTER PROMPT

## YOUR ROLE

Act as a senior full-stack engineer, integration specialist, QA engineer, and security reviewer.

Your job is to inspect, integrate, debug, and test the existing PersonaShiftAI application using the code already committed to the GitHub repository.

This is an existing hackathon project. The frontend and backend have already been developed independently and pushed to separate branches.

**Do not start a new project from scratch. Do not replace the existing application with a new template. Do not assume that either implementation is correct without inspecting it.**

Your primary goal is to make the existing frontend and backend work together reliably, verify that real AI rewriting works, and prepare a demo-ready application.

Repository: https://github.com/goyalanshika2507-dot/undefined-core.git

Branches: Frontend: frontend, Backend: feat/backend-api

Team: Agrim: Frontend, Dilbahar: Backend, Shreya: Backend, Anshika: Integration.

You are performing Anshika integration and testing responsibilities.

TASK: Integrate Ecoglow Authentication into Undefined-core (Persona AI)
Act as a senior full-stack developer. Your task is to integrate the authentication experience from the existing Ecoglow website into my current project, Undefined-core (VibeShift), and connect it to my new Supabase project.
1. SOURCE WEBSITE
Reference website:
[https://ecoglow-j9lju9e7b-goyalanshika2507-dots-projects.vercel.app](https://ecoglow-j9lju9e7b-goyalanshika2507-dots-projects.vercel.app/)
Vercel deployment details:
[https://vercel.com/goyalanshika2507-dots-projects/ecoglow/4Ln8egjuf7m5E8oT3CpvW1bn7aXj](https://vercel.com/goyalanshika2507-dots-projects/ecoglow/4Ln8egjuf7m5E8oT3CpvW1bn7aXj)
First, inspect the reference website and identify its complete authentication experience, including:
Login and sign-up screens.
Form fields and validation.
Password visibility toggle, if available.
Password recovery, if available.
Loading states and error messages.
Navigation between authentication screens.
Responsive layout and mobile behavior.
Any authentication-related redirects or user session handling.
Use the reference website as the design and behavior reference. Do not blindly copy its branding or unrelated application features.
If the deployed website does not expose its source code or complete authentication flow, inspect the accessible UI and existing local project files. Do not invent unavailable features or claim that you copied code you could not access.
2. TARGET PROJECT
The target project is the currently opened local repository:
Undefined-core /PersonaAI
Before making changes:
Inspect the complete project structure.
Read package.json and identify the existing frontend and backend architecture.
Inspect the current authentication implementation, if any.
Inspect existing routes, components, API services, environment files, and dependencies.
Review the current Git branch and working-tree status.
Identify which files are already modified and preserve the existing work.
The project uses React, Vite, JavaScript, and Tailwind CSS on the frontend, with a Node.js/Express backend and Google Gemini integration.
Verify the actual files before assuming that every part of this stack is already implemented.
3. AUTHENTICATION UI AND THEME
Recreate the authentication experience of the Ecoglow reference website as closely as reasonably possible in terms of functionality and layout.
However, adapt the styling to the existing VibeShift identity.
VibeShift's core promise is:
"Same intent. Better communication."
The authentication pages should feel like a natural part of VibeShift, not like a separate Ecoglow application.
Requirements:
Use VibeShift branding and appropriate application copy.
Match the existing VibeShift typography, colors, spacing, buttons, and visual language.
Maintain a polished, modern, responsive design.
Ensure desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts work correctly.
Reuse existing components and styling conventions where practical.
Use the existing icon library if suitable; do not add unnecessary dependencies.
Preserve the current application's existing pages and functionality.
Do not redesign unrelated pages.
Do not replace the entire application with a new template.
Implement only the authentication-related screens and components needed for the requested integration.
4. SUPABASE PROJECT CONFIGURATION
My new Supabase project details are:
Project name: Undefined-core
Project ID: mjzlfchmimnacgrotkkc
Use this project for the target application's authentication and any required authentication-related database configuration.
Important:
The project ID alone is not sufficient to initialize the Supabase client. Obtain the correct Project URL and publishable key from the project's official configuration or from environment variables that I have already configured.
Do not guess these values.
If you cannot access the configuration, tell me exactly which values I need to obtain and where to put them.
Security requirements:
Never hardcode credentials in source files.
Never expose the Supabase secret/service-role key in frontend code.
Never expose the Gemini API key in frontend code.
Keep the existing Gemini API integration intact.
Keep secret environment files out of Git.
Check that .env is ignored by Git.
Update .env.example with placeholder values only, if necessary.
Never print actual secrets in terminal output, logs, reports, or source files.
Use the existing Supabase package if it is already installed. Otherwise, install the minimum required dependency.
Configure the Supabase client using the existing project conventions. Avoid creating multiple conflicting Supabase clients.
5. AUTHENTICATION FUNCTIONALITY
Implement the authentication features supported by the reference experience and compatible with the existing application.
Where applicable, implement:
User registration.
User login.
Logout.
Password validation and confirmation.
Appropriate loading and error states.
Session persistence using Supabase's supported authentication behavior.
Session restoration when the user refreshes the page.
Password recovery if supported by the reference flow.
Appropriate redirects after successful login and registration.
Protected application routes where required.
A sensible unauthenticated-user experience.
Use Supabase Auth for real authentication. Do not create fake login functionality or hardcode test credentials.
Do not store plaintext passwords in the database or localStorage.
Do not add Google/GitHub OAuth or phone OTP authentication unless the existing reference experience or explicit project requirements call for it.
If email confirmation is enabled in Supabase, handle the confirmation flow properly instead of assuming every registration immediately produces an authenticated session.
6. ROUTING AND APPLICATION INTEGRATION
Inspect the current routing configuration before implementing authentication.
Integrate the authentication screens into the existing routing structure without breaking existing VibeShift pages.
Use sensible routes such as /login and /signup only if they fit the current application.
After authentication:
Redirect users to the appropriate existing application page.
Preserve existing rewrite-tool functionality.
Handle unauthenticated access to protected routes appropriately.
Handle logout and session expiration gracefully.
Do not invent a dashboard or replace the current homepage unless required by the existing project structure.
7. DATABASE AND SUPABASE SETUP
Inspect whether the project actually requires custom database tables for authentication.
Use Supabase Auth for identity management. Do not create a separate password-storage system.
If the application needs a user profile table:
Create only the necessary schema.
Use the authenticated user's ID as the appropriate relationship to the Supabase Auth user.
Configure appropriate Row Level Security (RLS) policies.
Ensure users cannot read or modify other users' private profile records.
Avoid storing unnecessary personal information.
Do not execute destructive SQL, delete existing tables, or overwrite database configuration.
If SQL setup is required, provide a migration or SQL file and clearly explain what needs to be run in the Supabase SQL Editor.
Do not claim that SQL or database changes have been applied unless you actually verified their execution.
8. BACKEND AND API COMPATIBILITY
The application has an AI-powered communication rewriting feature.
Preserve the existing rewrite API and its request/response contract.
Do not break:
POST /api/rewrite
GET /api/health
Verify the actual current implementation before modifying either endpoint.
Do not unnecessarily move existing Gemini API logic into the frontend.
Do not require authentication for unrelated endpoints unless the current project requirements explicitly demand it.
If authentication checks are needed for backend endpoints, implement them securely and validate Supabase access tokens server-side.
9. TESTING
After implementing the changes:
Install only the necessary dependencies.
Run the project's existing tests where available.
Run the production build.
Fix errors introduced by your changes.
Test registration and login flows.
Test invalid credentials and form validation.
Test logout and session restoration.
Test route protection and redirects.
Verify that the authentication UI is responsive.
Verify that the existing VibeShift rewriting interface still works.
Verify that the existing backend endpoints remain functional.
Check for exposed credentials and accidental .env tracking.
Do not claim a feature works unless you have tested it or clearly state what remains unverified.
10. IMPLEMENTATION RULES
Work inside the existing repository.
Preserve unrelated files and existing user changes.
Do not delete working features.
Do not overwrite files without inspecting them first.
Avoid unnecessary refactoring.
Avoid unnecessary package installations.
Do not create duplicate components, API clients, or configuration files.
Do not modify the Git remote or switch repositories.
Do not push to GitHub automatically.
Do not commit automatically.
Never expose API keys or secrets.
If an essential configuration value or decision is missing, explain the exact blocker instead of guessing.
11. FINAL REPORT
When finished, provide a concise report containing:
Authentication features implemented.
Files created or modified.
Supabase configuration completed.
Any required environment variables.
Any SQL or dashboard configuration I must complete manually.
Tests and build results.
Known limitations or unverified functionality.
Exact commands to run the application locally.
First inspect the repository and plan the smallest safe set of changes. Then implement the integration, verify it, and report the actual results.                 ## 10. STRICT LOCAL TESTING ONLY ? DO NOT COMMIT OR PUSH

IMPORTANT: This task is strictly for local development, experimentation, and testing.

**DO NOT COMMIT OR PUSH ANY CHANGES TO GITHUB.**

Follow these rules without exception:

1. Make all code changes only in the currently opened local project.
2. Do not run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`, `git pull`, `git merge`, or `git rebase`.
3. Do not create, delete, rename, or switch Git branches.
4. Do not modify the Git remote URL or repository settings.
5. Do not create or merge Pull Requests.
6. Do not upload code, files, environment variables, or credentials to GitHub.
7. Do not automatically publish or deploy the project to Vercel or any other hosting platform.
8. Do not overwrite, delete, or discard my existing uncommitted changes.
9. Preserve all existing files and unrelated project functionality.
10. Do not commit `.env` files, API keys, Supabase credentials, or other secrets.
11. You may install required dependencies and run the application locally for testing.
12. You may edit code, run tests, run the development server, and run a production build locally.
13. If Git operations appear necessary, STOP and ask me for permission instead of executing them.

### Final verification

After implementing the authentication integration:

* Run the relevant tests and local build.
* Report which files were created or modified.
* Explain any configuration steps I must complete manually.
* Tell me whether the application runs successfully locally.
* Clearly state any remaining errors or unverified functionality.

**FINAL RULE: Keep every change local. This task is for testing only. Do not push or commit anything to GitHub, even if the implementation is complete. I will decide separately when and whether to commit or push the changes.**
